question.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} & =3{b}_{3}-{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}, \\ {c}_{2} & =4{b}_{2}-5{b}_{1}, \\ {c}_{3} & =2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}a & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & b & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & c\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $C$ relative to the basis $B$ are

$$
[{c}_{1}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[{c}_{2}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[{c}_{3}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=-1,$ $b=4,$ and $c=3.$
